title: The local Langlands correspondence for G₂: theta lifting, triality and Kret–Shin parameters
summary: Construct the local Langlands map for the split exceptional group G₂ over characteristic-zero nonarchimedean fields through exceptional theta lifting, classical packets, triality and spin-valued Galois representations. Determine its enhanced fibres and analytic characterizations, and build the weak PGSp₆ correspondence from standard and spin transfers. Keep the cubic selfdual packets, the induced Siegel spin comparison and the omitted proper-Levi cases explicit, with the exact residual-characteristic and globalization hypotheses.
readme:
# The local Langlands correspondence for G₂

The aim is a reusable construction of the parameter map for split G₂ and its packet enhancements, together with the standard/spin comparisons that produce a weak correspondence for PGSp₆. The main G₂ endpoint is a finite-to-one surjection. At residue characteristic three the discrete A₂ packets retain the paper’s possible exception; the subregular packet is complete. The PGSp₆ endpoint assigns weak classes determined by two transfers and does not assert a full enhanced LLC outside the exceptional discrete locus.

Fix a nonarchimedean local field F of characteristic zero, with residue characteristic p, a nontrivial smooth additive character ψ, a Whittaker datum and compatible local reciprocity and unitary induction normalizations. Write WD_F=W_F×SL₂(ℂ). An admissible parameter is continuous on W_F, Frobenius-semisimple there, and algebraic on SL₂. A parameter class always means conjugacy by the named dual group, not arbitrary GL-conjugacy. Boundedness is imposed on the Weil image; discreteness means nonfactorization through a proper dual Levi. Retain the nilpotent monodromy operator in every Frobenius-semisimplified WD comparison.

Use j:SL₃→G₂, i:G₂→Spin₇, q:Spin₇→SO₇, v=q∘i and s:Spin₇→GL₈. The G₂ component group is the raw π₀ centralizer because its centre is trivial. Split PGSp₆ enhancements instead use the Spin₇ component group modulo the image of its central μ₂. A quadratic twist of a PGSp₆ representation uses its similitude modulo squares; the corresponding parameter twist is central in Spin₇. Quadratic-character homogeneous sets can have nontrivial stabilizers.

For G₂, the exceptional supplier’s spade locus lifts to PD×, the heart locus to PGSp₆, the club locus is the part of the heart lifting also to PGL₃⋊⟨duality⟩, and diamond is the rest of the heart. For classical PGSp₆ theta in LG.8–LG.10, the same symbols refer to the *classical* split/anisotropic orthogonal towers. They are different partitions on different representation spaces. Their definitions and duality theorems are imported from their respective owners. The discrete diamond G₂ parameters are those outside the discrete A₂ image.

The main theorem is assembled in LG.7. Its enhanced PGSp₆ theta application is restricted to diamond discrete parameters. The generic-discrete spin diagram has generic **tempered** PGSp₆ as its intermediate codomain: the generic G₂ subregular member lifts to a proper Siegel-induced constituent. LG.5 proves the diamond identity and specifies the separate club calculation. LG.10 assembles the weak correspondence only after the explicit proper-Levi and lower-tower obligations of LG.9–LG.10.

## Existing foundations and ownership

The baseline is Tau Ceti `f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369` and Mathlib `082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174`. Matrix diagonalization and characteristic polynomials supply the concrete torus checks. Mathlib’s spinGroup is an existing Clifford-algebra submonoid; it does not by itself provide the pinned dual-group/parameter models needed here. No absent Langlands carrier is simulated in the suggested Lean file.

The current TauCetiRoadmap main was also read at `0d144d044dacebca17b654695b6f1ad58f159b27`, and current Tau Ceti at `a91d3aafa8cd3e6bc33dfde0d7677ed0f1625039`. ReductiveGroups, RepresentationTheory/ClassicalGroups, RepresentationTheory/SpinRepresentations and the newer OrthogonalSpinGroups roadmap own the group and Clifford foundations. In particular, `TauCeti.D4Tripled.trialityAutomorphism` is an integral group-scheme automorphism, with root-subgroup and order-three theorems, not just a diagram permutation. Reuse it; LG.2 owns only the rational model comparison, central quotient descent and its theta application. The G₂ short-root root-datum carrier is also existing current work; its own documentation separates explicit torus/root data from identification with a separately defined reductive group. No group classification or general spinor-norm project is planned here.

The reviewed library coverage for AL.3–AL.4 (AUDIT-14) and MP.3 (AUDIT-15) reports the relevant analytic/parameter/theta theory absent, while recognizing existing matrix polynomial and abstract coinvariant support. The new roadmap has no reviewed audit of its own. Missing audit entries under the current ML, ET and SR ids are not evidence of absence. Searches of the pinned and current Tau Ceti trees found no exceptional LLC, WD parameter, Xu packet or automorphic theta carrier; the actual current Lie/Spin declarations were then inspected to avoid duplicating them.

Kret–Shin Theorem A, Chenevier Theorem E and Theorem 6.4, the independent gamma characterization and Shin Theorem 5.8 are stated below with their published hypotheses. They are source-gated contracts with named proof-ownership gaps, not axioms silently added to a claimed closed graph. Likewise the Arthur/Xu supplier’s unclosed trace-formula inputs propagate to every dependent endpoint.


Two source comparisons require particular care. Kret–Shin Proposition 13.1(4), PDF pp. 60–61 (journal pp. 134–135), proves spin Galois irreducibility under the full Steinberg, cohomological and spin-regular hypotheses. It supports the special globalization’s GL₈ cuspidality after algebraic-summand comparison; the general spin transfer is still isobaric. Shin’s Corollary 4.12, author PDF p. 24, permits the explicit PGSp₆ weight sequence λ_t=t(8,4,2); its shifted coordinates h=(8t+3,4t+2,2t+1) have eight distinct spin weights and satisfy the density growth condition.

stages.title: Dual groups, conjugacy and parameter detection
stages.description: Fix the standard inclusions j:SL₃(ℂ)→G₂(ℂ), i:G₂(ℂ)→Spin₇(ℂ), q:Spin₇(ℂ)→SO₇(ℂ), the vector representation v=q∘i, and the eight-dimensional spin representation s. The kernels are ker(j)=ker(i)=ker(v)=1 and ker(q)=μ₂. Their induced maps on admissible parameter conjugacy classes use these fixed embeddings, not arbitrary identifications of abstract groups. For a,b∈ℂˣ define A₂ vector eigenvalues d₇(a,b)=(1,a,b,(ab)⁻¹,a⁻¹,b⁻¹,ab), D₇=diag(d₇), and D₈=diag(1,d₇). Define P₇=charpoly(D₇). This is a concrete torus calculation for the restriction v∘j, not a definition of G₂ or of its parameters. v∘j≅1⊕Std₃⊕Std₃∨ and s∘i≅1⊕v. Under Spin₇→Spin₈, the eight-dimensional vector representation restricts to 1⊕q and each half-spin representation restricts to s. Each equality is an isomorphism of algebraic representations, hence also of composed Weil–Deligne representations. j induces an injection Φ(PGL₃)/(τ↦τ∨)→Φ(G₂). For a discrete G₂ parameter φ, its class lies in this image exactly when L(s,vφ) has a pole at s=0. If φ=jφτ with φτ discrete, Sφ=π₀Z_G₂(φ) is μ₃ when φτ is not self-dual and S₃ when φτ is self-dual. i_*:Φ(G₂)→Φ(PGSp₆) is injective. On discrete φ outside the A₂ image (the diamond locus), iφ is discrete, its spin L-factor has a pole at zero, and conversely a discrete Spin₇ parameter with that pole is iφ for a unique diamond φ. For such φ, i induces Sφ≅S_{iφ}/image Z(Spin₇). v_*:Φ(G₂)→Φ(GL₇) is injective on conjugacy classes. It carries the diamond discrete locus into the discrete SO₇ parameters; it is not asserted to carry every G₂-discrete parameter into an irreducible GL₇ parameter. Let ρ:Γ→G₂(ℂ) be completely reducible and χ:Γ→{±1} nontrivial. If iρ and χ·iρ are not Spin₇-conjugate, then (vρ)⊗χ has no invariant vector. In particular, if s(χ·iρ)≅1⊕vρ, then χ·iρ is conjugate to iρ. For Spin₇ parameters φ,φ′ put φ∼wφ′ exactly when qφ≅qφ′ as SO₇ parameters and sφ≅sφ′ as GL₈ parameters. Define Φw(PGSp₆)=Φ(PGSp₆)/∼w. These are conjugacy classes of WD parameters before taking the additional quotient. Two admissible Spin₇(ℂ) parameters are weakly equivalent exactly when their values at every element of W_F×SL₂(ℂ) are Spin₇-conjugate. This relation can be strictly weaker than conjugacy by a single element. Let k be totally real and A a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL₇(A_k), regular algebraic at every real place. The following are equivalent: almost every Satake parameter of A lies in v(G₂(ℂ)); at every finite place u the full local parameter of A_u has a unique G₂-valued lift modulo G₂-conjugacy. Translate Chenevier’s W×SU₂ convention to algebraic W×SL₂ without discarding monodromy. For the same k,A satisfying the almost-everywhere G₂ Satake condition, a coefficient field E, a prime ℓ and λ|ℓ of E, the associated semisimple r_{A,λ}:G_k→GL₇(Ē_λ) is v∘r̃ for a continuous semisimple r̃:G_k→G₂(Ē_λ), unique up to G₂-conjugacy. Semisimple means reductive identity component of the Zariski closure. This is not an independent all-places local–global compatibility theorem. Let Γ=μ₄×μ₄ with projection characters a,b and let V have characters {a,ab²,b,ba²}; det V=1 gives r:Γ→SU₄=Spin₆→Spin₇. Put η=b². Then r and ηr are elementwise Spin₇-conjugate and have isomorphic standard and spin representations, but are not conjugate by one Spin₇ element. This is a finite-group test of the weak quotient; it is not claimed to be a pair of KS parameters of one automorphic representation.

stages.title: Globalization with periods and Whittaker models
stages.description: Let k be totally real, O a totally definite octonion k-algebra split at every finite place, G=Aut(O), and D⊂O a quaternion subalgebra. Let G_D fix D pointwise. Inside L²(G(k)\G(A_k)), L²_D is the orthogonal complement of the closed span of automorphic representations all of whose vectors have zero G_D(k)\G_D(A_k)-period. The period uses the fixed quotient measure. For split simple G/k, a global Whittaker character ψ, a finite place w and a generic supercuspidal σ of G(k_w), let L²_{ψ-gen,σ} be the orthogonal complement, inside the σ-isotypic cuspidal L² part at w, of the closed span of copies on which the global ψ-Whittaker functional vanishes. It is the globally generic selected spectrum with this exact local component. Its Hilbert decomposition retains the surviving automorphic multiplicities; local Whittaker models alone do not define it. In the quaternion-period setting, the prescribed product of local distinguished representations is weakly contained in the restriction of L²_D. In the Whittaker setting with fixed supercuspidal σ at w, products of generic square-integrable local representations, together with hyperspecial vectors away from the prescribed places and one auxiliary place, are weakly contained in L²_{ψ-gen,σ}. The local embeddings and support conditions are part of the input. For a nonempty finite set S of finite places of totally real k, prescribe π_u on split G₂(k_u), each supercuspidal with nonzero PGSp₆ theta lift or Steinberg, and prescribe any irreducible finite-dimensional representation of compact G₂(k_u) at each real u. There are D⊂O and an automorphic Π of Aut(O) with those exact local components and nonzero D-period. For Π constructed by quaternion-period globalization, its global theta lift to split PGSp₆ is nonzero. It is cuspidal if a prescribed finite component is Steinberg, or a prescribed real highest weight is regular. Its local components are the nonzero local theta lifts. Let δ be a generic discrete series of G₂(F) whose PGSp₆ theta lift is also discrete series. Fix an auxiliary generic supercuspidal σ whose PGSp₆ theta lift is supercuspidal. Then δ is isolated among irreducible G₂(F) representations occurring locally in the globally generic cuspidal spectrum with auxiliary component σ. For split simple G over a number field, prescribe generic discrete series at finitely many places, each isolated among local components of the fixed-supercuspidal globally generic family. Then there is a globally generic cuspidal automorphic representation with those components and spherical components outside that finite set and at most one further finite place. Specify the auxiliary generic supercuspidal in the fixed family as part of the prescribed data.

stages.title: Triality and the generic spin transfer
stages.description: For split D₄ over F construct the natural central isogeny f₁:SO₈→PGSO₈ and its two triality companions f₂,f₃. Their dual maps identify the vector representation and the two half-spin representations of Spin₈. Reuse the integral pinned D₄ triality automorphism already in current Tau Ceti; this target is its comparison, central quotient descent and compatibility with these F-rational group models. For generic σ∈Irr(PGSp₆(F)), take its nonzero classical theta lift to PGSO₈(F), pull back along f₂, choose a constituent modulo the even-orthogonal outer automorphism, and apply Arthur’s standard transfer to GL₈. This defines SpinLift(σ), independent of that choice and of choosing f₂ or f₃. If a cuspidal Σ on PGSp₆(A_k) has nonzero cuspidal classical theta lift to PGSO₈, apply triality and the global Arthur standard transfer. The result SpinLift(Σ) is an isobaric automorphic representation of GL₈ with the local SpinLift(Σ_u) at generic finite places, and with the corresponding triality-theta transfer at the remaining places. Isobaricity is the conclusion; cuspidality needs a separate argument. For generic discrete-series σ of PGSp₆(F), the Langlands–Shahidi gamma factor γ(s,σ,spin,ψ) equals the standard GL₈ gamma factor of SpinLift(σ). The convention is the unitary automorphic normalization, with the same nontrivial ψ and compatible Haar measures. For generic discrete-series σ and a quadratic χ:F×→{±1}, SpinLift(σ⊗χ∘sim)≅SpinLift(σ)⊗χ∘det. Here sim on PGSp₆ means its class modulo squares. The same identity for general generic tempered Siegel lifts is a separate explicit-theta calculation used by the club bridge.

stages.title: The G₂ parameter map and its characterizations
stages.description: If π has nonzero exceptional theta lift θ(π) to PGSp₆(F), the local Langlands parameter assigned by Arthur to rest θ(π) is vφ for a unique φ∈Φ(G₂). The restriction is an orbit of Sp₆ constituents under PGSp₆(F), not a chosen constituent without conjugacy control. Use the exceptional theta dichotomy Irr(G₂)=Irr♠⊔Irr♥. On Irr♠ set L(π)=j rec_PD×(θ_Dπ), using the degree-three division algebra and JL. On Irr♥ let L(π) be the unique G₂ parameter whose v-image is rec_Sp₆(rest θπ). The definition is on representation isomorphism classes. Decompose Irr♥=Irr♣⊔Irr♦ by whether the PGL₃⋊⟨duality⟩ lift is nonzero. On Irr♣ define L_B(π)=j rec_PGL₃(τ), where τ is the underlying PGL₃ constituent of that lift, determined up to duality. On Irr♠ and Irr♦ retain the division and PGSp₆ definitions respectively. L_B=L. More explicitly, if π=θ_B(τ±), then rec_Sp₆(rest θπ)=v j rec_PGL₃(τ), including reducible tempered Siegel inductions and non-tempered Langlands quotients. For every non-tempered π=J_P^G₂(τ), with τ the standard essentially tempered inducing data in a proper Levi, Lπ is rec_M(τ) followed by M∨→G₂∨. This gives a bijection between non-tempered representations and non-tempered parameter classes. The proper Levis are the two copies of GL₂ and the split rank-two torus. π is tempered exactly when Lπ has bounded Weil image. If π is a constituent of normalized induction from a unitary discrete series τ of a proper Levi M, then Lπ is the composite of rec_M(τ) with the dual Levi embedding. π is square-integrable precisely when Lπ does not factor through a proper dual Levi. This condition concerns the full WD parameter, and allows a nontrivial Deligne SL₂. Every bounded non-discrete φ has a fibre of cardinality |Irr(Sφ)|, equal to one or two. The packet has a unique generic member labelled by the trivial character. This statement holds also at p=3. Define Lif(π)∈Irr(GL₇(F)) by the Arthur transfer of rest θπ on Irr♥, and by the GL₇ LLC representation of φτ⊕1⊕φτ∨ on Irr♠, where τ=JL(θ_Dπ). Thus rec_GL₇(Lifπ)=vLπ. The direct-sum prescription is used even when a written parabolic induction is reducible. For ψ nontrivial and smooth additive on F, π∈Irr(G₂) and τ∈Irr(GL_r), define γ_G₂(s,π×τ,ψ)=γ_RS(s,Lif(π)×τ,ψ). It is a meromorphic function, using the normalized Rankin–Selberg factor and the same additive character on both sides. GF Theorem 2.4 uniquely characterizes these local nonarchimedean factors by cuspidal-support multiplicativity and a restricted global functional equation. The G₂ torus rule uses 1⊕⊕χ_i^{±1}; the P-Levi rule uses φτ⊕φτ∨⊕detφτ⊕detφτ⁻¹⊕1; the Q-Levi rule uses φτ⊕φτ∨⊕Adφτ. The GL_r rule is multiplicativity under parabolic induction. Globally k is totally real, G=Aut(O), Π is cuspidal and spherical at every split real place, T is cuspidal on GL_r, and either Π has nonzero cuspidal theta lift to split PGSp₆ or nonzero lift to PD× for a degree-three central simple algebra (possibly split). For S containing infinity and all ramification of Π,T,ψ, the partial tensor L-function continues meromorphically and satisfies L^S(1−s,Π×T∨)=∏_{u∈S}γ_u(s,Π_u×T_u,ψ_u) L^S(s,Π×T). For every π, τ and ψ as above, γ_G₂(s,π×τ,ψ)=γ(s,(vLπ)⊗rec_GL_r(τ),ψ). The comparison is between meromorphic functions, with full WD monodromy and matching reciprocity conventions. The map L is uniquely determined by discrete-series detection, tempered induction, non-tempered Langlands quotients, and preservation of the preceding pair gamma factors for all GL_r twists. For bounded seven-dimensional WD representations arising here, equality of these factors for all twists implies isomorphism. A map Irr(G₂)→Φ(G₂) satisfying Main Theorem (i)–(iv), with the fixed normalizations above, equals L. The two theta branches determine the parameter by injectivity of j modulo duality and injectivity of v. Let k be totally real and Π be globally generic, regular algebraic and cuspidal on split G₂, with a Steinberg finite component. Any semisimple associated rank-seven Galois representation with the prescribed almost-everywhere Satake classes has a unique G₂-valued lift up to G₂-conjugacy. At every finite place u its full Frobenius-semisimplified WD parameter is L(Π_u), after the fixed coefficient-field identification. At u|ℓ require the potentially semistable comparison with its precise algebraic normalization.

stages.title: A₂ packets and cubic inner forms
stages.description: Use inv:H¹(F,PGL₃)≅(1/3)ℤ/ℤ and the Kottwitz pairing with Z(SL₃)=μ₃. Label M₃(F), D₁, D₂ by 0,1/3,2/3, so their characters of μ₃ are 1,χ,χ⁻¹. For a discrete PGL₃ parameter use JL to obtain the representations of PD₁× and PD₂×; opposite algebra and contragredient interchange the two nontrivial labels. The algebras and general invariant map are imported, not redefined. Let φ=jφτ be discrete with φτ not self-dual, so Sφ=μ₃. The split theta lift gives the unique generic member with label 1; the two cubic inner-form lifts give labels χ,χ⁻¹. For p≠3 these give a bijection L⁻¹(φ)≅Irr(μ₃). For p=3 retain the canonical injection and do not claim all nontrivial labels occur. Let φ=jφτ be discrete and φτ self-dual, so Sφ≅S₃. Construct and verify the packet bijection with {1,sgn,std₂} for p≠3, with the generic member labelled 1. The two split τ± lifts account for the two labels restricting trivially to μ₃; the division-algebra lift accounts for std₂, whose restriction is χ⊕χ⁻¹. For p=3 prove the stated injection; prove bijectivity in the subregular SL₂ case separately. For the parameter with trivial Weil part and subregular SL₂ in G₂, Sφ=S₃ and the packet is {π_gen[1],π_sc[1],π_deg[1]} labelled {1,sgn,std₂}, respectively. The split St_PGL₃⁺ and St_PGL₃⁻ lift to the first two; the trivial PD× representation lifts to π_deg[1]. This packet is complete also at p=3. Assume p≠3. For τ∈Irr(PGL₃), the set of irreducible lifts from τ and τ∨ is exactly the enhanced G₂ representations (jφτ,η) with η trivial on the image of π₀Z_SL₃(φτ). For τ discrete and its division JL transfer, the division theta lifts are exactly those with η nontrivial on that image. In the selfdual discrete case this means {1,sgn} on the split side and std₂ on the division side.

stages.title: Kret–Shin parameters and exceptional spin compatibility
stages.description: Let k be totally real, n≥2 and Σ cuspidal on GSp_{2n}(A_k). Assume (St): a finite component is a character twist of Steinberg; and (L-coh): Σ∞|sim|^{-n(n+1)/4} is ξ-cohomological for an irreducible algebraic ξ of Res_{k/ℚ}GSp_{2n}. For each ℓ and ℂ≅Q̄_ℓ there is a continuous GSpin_{2n+1}-valued ρΣ, unique up to conjugacy in the sense of Theorem A, whose SO quotient is the Galois representation of the Sp restriction and whose Gm quotient is the central character by class field theory. Outside rational primes 2, ramification of k or Σ, and ℓ, Frobenius semisimple classes match unramified Satake. At ℓ it is de Rham with the prescribed Hodge cocharacter and the crystalline/semistable qualifications of Theorem A(iii). For central-trivial Σ and n=3 it lands in Spin₇; the exponent in (L-coh) is −3. Let k be totally real and Σ cuspidal on PGSp₆(A_k). Assume the (St) and (L-coh) hypotheses of Kret–Shin and (spin-REG): the spin parameter is regular at every real place. For each coefficient prime and coefficient-field identification, the eight-dimensional spin representation sρΣ of the Kret–Shin Spin₇-valued Galois representation is absolutely irreducible. For generic discrete-series σ of PGSp₆, a KS parameter is a discrete Spin₇ parameter φ satisfying qφ=rec_Sp₆(rest σ) and sφ=rec_GL₈(SpinLift σ). This is a set of parameter classes; existence and singleton assertions are separate theorems. Every generic discrete-series σ of PGSp₆ has a KS parameter. Any two have the same q-image and differ, after conjugacy, by a quadratic character of W_F; no general singleton conclusion follows. If π is generic discrete series on the G₂ diamond locus and σ=θπ, then σ is generic discrete series and its KS parameter set consists of the single class iLπ. For generic discrete-series π in Irr♦(G₂), rec_GL₈(SpinLift θπ)=s i Lπ=1⊕vLπ. Let π be generic discrete series in Irr♣(G₂), coming from a discrete τ of PGL₃ with φτ. HD Theorem 15.2 gives θπ=I₃(τ) when τ is not selfdual, and θπ=I₃(τ)_gen when τ is selfdual. Compute the classical theta lift and its triality transfer to prove rec_GL₈(SpinLift θπ)=φτ⊕φτ∨⊕1⊕1=s i j φτ. This includes the generic subregular representation π_gen[1]. For every generic discrete-series π of G₂, θπ is nonzero generic tempered and rec_GL₈(SpinLift θπ)=s iLπ. On the diamond locus θπ is discrete series; on the club locus it is a proper Siegel-induced tempered representation.

stages.title: Diamond fibres and distinguished Xu packets
stages.description: For each φ∈Φ♦_ds(G₂), there is a generic discrete-series π with Lπ=φ. Thus the diamond parameter map is surjective for every residue characteristic. For φ∈Φ♦_ds(G₂), L⁻¹(φ) has exactly one generic member. Equivalently, among generic PGSp₆ representations whose standard restriction has parameter q iφ, exactly one has nonzero G₂ theta lift. For diamond discrete φ, put φ♭=q iφ and let X*(φ) be the unique Xu packet over φ♭ containing θπ_gen, where π_gen is the unique generic member of L⁻¹(φ). It is a packet of representations, distinguished by a point, rather than a chosen lift of φ♭ without a rule. For π in a diamond discrete fibre, choose totally real k with k_{w₁}≅k_{w₂}≅F and globalize π at both places to Π with nonzero cuspidal PGSp₆ theta lift Σ. For generic π use the split G₂ form, an auxiliary generic depth-zero supercuspidal whose theta lift is supercuspidal, and archimedean discrete series far enough from the walls. For nongeneric π, which is supercuspidal here, use the definite octonion form and a Steinberg finite place. In each case the Sp₆ global parameter of Σ is generic. For any Xu packet over φ♭=q iφ with φ diamond discrete, either every member has nonzero local theta lift to split G₂ or no member does. Exceptional theta induces a bijection L⁻¹(φ)↔X*(φ) for each diamond discrete φ. No other Xu packet over φ♭ participates in G₂ theta. Compose theta L⁻¹(φ)≅X*(φ), Xu’s Whittaker-normalized labelling X*(φ)≅Irr(S_{iφ}/image μ₂), and the dual-group isomorphism Sφ≅S_{iφ}/image μ₂. This gives the enhancement bijection L⁻¹(φ)≅Irr(Sφ) for diamond discrete φ at every p.

stages.title: The G₂ correspondence and enhanced theta applications
stages.description: L:Irr(G₂(F))→Φ(G₂) is a natural surjective map with finite fibres. It satisfies discrete-series detection, tempered induction and Langlands-quotient compatibility, the two defining theta diagrams, both uniqueness characterizations, the corrected generic-discrete spin identity, and pair-gamma compatibility. Every fibre is in natural bijection with Irr(Sφ) if p≠3; at p=3 this holds outside possibly the discrete A₂ image, where a canonical injection is the general target and the subregular packet is still complete. For tempered φ the trivial label is its unique generic member. The global–local assertion has the hypotheses of LG.3/global-compatibility. L restricts to a bijection between generic supercuspidal G₂ representations and discrete G₂ parameters trivial on Deligne SL₂. This recovers the HKT correspondence through theta and triality, without importing potential modularity or automorphic descent as new prerequisites. Fix diamond discrete φ, write φ♭=q iφ, and consider all Xu packets over φ♭ and all Spin₇ lifts of φ♭. Each is a homogeneous set for quadratic characters; match the distinguished packet X*(φ) with iφ and extend equivariantly. Xu’s equality of stabilizers makes this a well-defined canonical bijection of homogeneous sets, with each packet labelled by Irr(S_{φ̃}/image μ₂). On diamond discrete φ, if π has enhancement (φ,η), then θπ has assigned parameter iφ and the Xu enhancement η′ satisfying η=η′∘i_* after the central quotient. This proves the Gross–Savin enhanced relation on Φ♦_ds(G₂); it does not assign enhanced PGSp₆ parameters for all G₂ representations.

stages.title: Classical discrete-series globalization and theta
stages.description: Let k be totally real, G connected reductive with discrete series at infinity, and A_G×ℝ=A_{G,ℝ}. Let S be finite, G unramified away from S and infinity, and Z(G)=1. For a relatively quasi-compact Plancherel-regular subset U of the local unitary dual at S with positive Plancherel measure, infinitely many cuspidal automorphic representations have S-component in U, are unramified outside S and infinity, and are discrete series at infinity. The theorem itself does not prescribe arbitrary spin-regular archimedean parameters. Let σ be discrete series of PGSp₆(F), k totally real with k_{v₀}≅F and v₁≠v₀ finite. There is cuspidal Σ of PGSp₆(A_k) with Σ_{v₀}=σ, Σ_{v₁}=St, generic cohomological spin-regular discrete series at every real place, and quadratic-unramified components at every other finite place. The prescribed σ is discrete series; this is not a globalization of arbitrary irreducibles. If σ in the preceding globalization lies in Irr♥(PGSp₆), then Θ(Σ) to split PGSO₈ is nonzero and cuspidal. Its local components are the nonzero local theta lifts. A Steinberg place has zero lower PGO₆ lift, so the tower property gives cuspidality at this first nonzero lift. For every discrete-series σ in Irr♥(PGSp₆), there exists a discrete Spin₇ parameter whose standard image is the local Langlands parameter assigned by Arthur to rest σ and whose spin image is the parameter of the triality-theta GL₈ transfer. Its weak class is unique.

stages.title: The extended spin transfer and all KS parameters
stages.description: Use the classical theta partition into Irr♠ and Irr♥, with Irr♣ the heart representations also lifting to split PGO₆. On the heart define SpinLift by the f₂ transform of θ♥ followed by Arthur transfer. On Irr♠♣ use θ♠♣ to PGL₂(D) or PGL₄, JL to a duality orbit of PGL₄, and attach the GL₈ representation with parameter φτ⊕φτ∨. The definitions must agree on the club overlap. For σ∈Irr♠♣, let τ be its PGL₄ theta/JL datum modulo duality, with φτ in SL₄=Spin₆. Under the fixed inclusion h:Spin₆→Spin₇, q hφτ≅1⊕Λ²φτ and s hφτ≅φτ⊕φτ∨. The first is the local Langlands parameter assigned by Arthur to rest σ and the second is the extended spin parameter. For each nondiscrete σ∈Irr♥, construct its Spin₇ parameter from the LLC of its proper Levi inducing data and prove simultaneously qφ=rec_Sp₆(rest σ) and sφ=rec_GL₈(SpinLift σ). Use the standard C₃ numbering α₁, α₂, α₃, with α₃ long. Cover the seven standard proper Levis indexed by ∅, {α₁}, {α₂}, {α₃}, {α₁,α₂}, {α₁,α₃}, {α₂,α₃}: the minimal torus, the three semisimple-rank-one refinements, and the maximal GL₃, GL₂×PGL₂ and GL₁×PGSp₄ types with their actual central quotients. Use the actual quotient Levi, normalized induction and Langlands quotient rather than an unjustified direct product identification. For every σ∈Irr(PGSp₆), there exists a unique class φ∈Φw(PGSp₆) with qφ=rec_Sp₆(rest σ) and sφ=rec_GL₈(SpinLift σ). Existence means that the two image parameters have a common admissible Spin₇ lift; uniqueness is in the weak quotient.

stages.title: The weak PGSp₆ correspondence and its fibres
stages.description: Define Lw(σ) to be the unique weak class of LG.9/all-ks. It is the unique map whose standard image is the local Langlands parameter assigned by Arthur to the Sp₆ restriction and whose spin image is the extended GL₈ spin-transfer parameter. Lw carries tempered representations to weak classes of bounded parameters and discrete series to weak classes of discrete parameters. The predicates are independent of the chosen representative of the weak class. This target states the forward implications of Theorem 12.6, without strengthening them to converses without proof. For σ∈Irr♥ and quadratic χ, SpinLift(σ⊗χ∘sim)=SpinLift(σ)⊗χ∘det. The similitude character on PGSO₈ modulo squares is trivial on f₁(SO₈(F)) and pulls back along f₂ to the spinor-norm character. Hence Lw(σ⊗χ)=Lw(σ)⊗χ. For σ∈Irr♠♣ and quadratic χ, its theta/JL PGL₄ datum becomes τ⊗χ∘det (using reduced norm on GL₂(D) before JL). Since χ²=1, (φτ⊗χ)⊕(φτ⊗χ)∨=(φτ⊕φτ∨)⊗χ, while Λ²(φτ⊗χ)=Λ²φτ. Therefore the extended spin lift twists by χ and Lw(σ⊗χ)=Lw(σ)⊗χ. Lw is surjective. For every weak class [φ], restriction gives a surjection Lw⁻¹([φ])→Π_{qφ}(Sp₆)/PGSp₆(F). In particular every orbit of a Sp₆ representation in that packet occurs in the fibre. Let σ be discrete series in the classical diamond locus (its parameter does not factor through Spin₆), and X the Xu packet containing it. Then Lw is constant on X. If a discrete parameter factors through Spin₆ and X is a Xu packet in the corresponding lower-tower locus, show that all σ∈X have the same extended spin parameter φτ⊕φτ∨ and hence the same Lw. Treat split and quaternionic theta lifts and their intersection with the heart separately. For every proper Levi of PGSp₆, prove the compatibility of its Xu packet induction and Langlands quotient with the two transfers defining Lw. Constancy on the discrete inducing packets must imply constancy on each tempered induced Xu packet, and on its non-tempered standard-module quotient packet. Include all proper-Levi types listed in LG.9/heart-levi-parameters. Every fibre of Lw is a union of complete Xu packets. For the weak class of iφ with φ diamond discrete G₂, the fibre is the single distinguished Xu packet X*(φ). No assertion of a full enhanced PGSp₆ LLC is made for general weak classes.
